requirement:
Only current results whose captured source inputs match the current source
and whose build configurations are compatible contribute counts to saved
execution-coverage checks under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`. Results with changed
inputs are identified as stale; results of unknown compatibility are
identified as unavailable. Both are excluded from combined totals.

A filtered run preserves the provenance of unselected results under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`. It does not make those
results fresh when their recorded inputs no longer match. Their process
reports and matching captured source remain available until replacement or
removal of the build artifacts.
rationale:
I judged the tests against each obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. I did not read implementation source. I found no gap.

- **Matching source inputs count.**
  - `source_and_build_inputs_invalidate_on_addition_removal_and_dirty_content` in `src/execution_coverage.rs` checks `fresh()` directly. It is true for the unchanged state. It turns false when source content changes, when files are added, when `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock` change, when a toolchain file appears, when watched directory inputs change, and when a missing watched input appears or a recorded file is removed. Each case is then restored and checked fresh again.
  - `real_build_captures_dependency_files_and_environment_for_read_only_freshness_checks` in `tests/execution_coverage.rs` runs a real build. It checks that include and build-script inputs are captured. Changing them makes the check report "stale coverage", and restoring them clears it. Retained files are unchanged afterwards, so the check is read-only.
- **Compatible build configuration.**
  - `cargo_launch_metadata_does_not_invalidate_but_caller_build_environment_does` in `src/execution_coverage/book.rs` shows that Cargo launch-time variables do not invalidate a record. It also shows that changing `CC`, `RUSTFLAGS`, `CARGO_PROFILE_*`, a Cargo target linker variable, or a fixture build variable does.
  - The same real-build test varies the compiler environment and build environment values.
  - `filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source` checks that a newer run with a different configuration (`build-b`) leaves only that run selected.
- **Stale results are identified as stale.** The tests assert "stale coverage" text and `fresh == false`:
  - `filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source`
  - `stale_or_unknown_records_publish_no_current_file_totals` in `src/execution_coverage/book.rs`
  - `inactive_and_stale_measurements_cannot_raise_the_file_total` in `src/execution_coverage/check.rs`
- **Unknown compatibility is identified as unavailable.**
  - `stale_or_unknown_records_publish_no_current_file_totals` sets an unsupported schema. It asserts a failing check with "cannot establish the current test set".
  - `inactive_and_stale_measurements_cannot_raise_the_file_total` sets a recorded configuration that disagrees with the active build. It asserts `invalid_store` and "active build configuration".
  - `unreadable_history_cannot_reintroduce_an_older_success` covers invalid metadata, missing source, unsupported schema and missing profile. It asserts a failed check and no positive counts, and that an older success is not revived.
  - The text does not fix wording for "unavailable", so these message assertions are adequate.
- **Both are excluded from combined totals.**
  - `stale_or_unknown_records_publish_no_current_file_totals` first shows `code.rs: 2/2 (100.0%) — pass` when fresh. After the source changes, and again with the unknown schema, it asserts that no `- code.rs:` line and no "100.0%" appear.
  - `inactive_and_stale_measurements_cannot_raise_the_file_total` has a stale success beside a fresh failure. It asserts that the stale result is not counted and no file totals are published.
- **Filtered run preserves provenance.**
  - `focused_recollection_leaves_only_the_unselected_result_stale_with_its_original_sources` re-runs one test after a source change.
  - The unselected result stays stale. Its attempt id, run id and original captured source (`fn a() {}`) are preserved, and the re-run result is fresh with the new source.
  - `stale_or_unknown_records_publish_no_current_file_totals` asserts that the SQLite store and the `.profraw` process report still exist after stale and unknown checks.

All the tests carry {test} references to the subject.

text: :::{req} index.freshness
Only current results whose captured source inputs match the current source
and whose build configurations are compatible contribute counts to saved
execution-coverage checks under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`. Results with changed
inputs are identified as stale; results of unknown compatibility are
identified as unavailable. Both are excluded from combined totals.
A filtered run preserves the provenance of unselected results under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`. It does not make those
results fresh when their recorded inputs no longer match. Their process
reports and matching captured source remain available until replacement or
removal of the build artifacts.
:::{req} index.selection
Saved execution-coverage checks read the current coverage set under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.current` from SQLite. Each check
uses one coherent database snapshot of test identities, states, provenance,
and processed measurements, so a replacement or update cannot mix results
from different snapshots within the same check.
Checks do not search historical runs or use a separate report-selection
metadata cache. Current test identities, states, and provenance can be read
without loading their detailed measurements.
Only current results with complete, available measurements contribute to
coverage under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`.
Pending, running, and unavailable entries are reported under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.measurement`. Checking does not build
or execute tests and never restores a superseded attempt.
:::{req} storage.replace
After preparation and selection discovery succeed, and before any selected
test starts, Habeas atomically establishes the new coverage set:
- An unfiltered workspace invocation clears the entire previous set,
including results for tests that no longer exist. This includes
`habeas coverage` with no supplied arguments and `habeas test`.
- An invocation with an explicit package or binary restriction, test filter,
partition, or ignored-only selection is filtered. It clears results for all
selected test identities and preserves unselected results within the
active build configuration.
- Every selected test receives a pending entry without measurements.
Native default filters and the default handling of ignored tests still apply
to an unfiltered workspace invocation. `--run-ignored all` alone does not make
a workspace invocation filtered.
A selected test that never starts because of fail-fast, interruption, or
execution startup failure remains unavailable. Its previous result does not
become available again. A filtered selection containing no tests leaves the
current results and active configuration unchanged; an empty unfiltered
workspace selection clears the previous set.
If the atomic replacement cannot be committed, the command reports the
failure and starts no tests. The previously committed coverage set and active
configuration remain unchanged.
